name: Aqara Presence Sensor FP2 (EU)

radios.note: 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi 802.11 b/g/n and Bluetooth 4.2. WPA/WPA2 enterprise networks are not supported.

matter.note: Aqara's FP2 pages we saw do not mention Matter, and an Aqara forum moderator says it does not support it. Not confirmed from a CSA listing either way.

apple_home.note: Connects over HomeKit with no hub. Aqara's manual says it appears as several separate sensors; third-party platforms get only basic sensor data.

google_home.note: Aqara lists Google Home with no hub needed. Aqara's manual says it appears as several separate sensors; third-party platforms get only basic sensor data.

alexa.note: Aqara lists Alexa with no hub needed. Aqara's manual says it appears as several separate sensors; third-party platforms get only basic sensor data.

smartthings.note: Samsung has a SmartThings catalogue page for the FP2, but Aqara's platform list omits SmartThings and we could not open Samsung's page to see how it connects.

home_assistant.note: Aqara says to add it with Home Assistant's HomeKit Device integration, with no Aqara hub. A device paired to Apple Home must be removed from there first.

hubRequired.note: Aqara's spec table says no hub is required. Full local automation needs an Aqara hub with Wi-Fi, per the manual.

localControl.note: HomeKit/Home Assistant control may stay on the local network but Aqara does not state local-only control.

senses.note: mmWave presence with multi-zone tracking (up to 5 people, up to 30 zones) and fall detection in ceiling mode; a built-in light sensor is also listed.

power.note: 5 V / 1 A over USB-C; no battery.

summary: Aqara Presence Sensor FP2 senses presence with mmWave, tracking up to 5 people across up to 30 zones, and has a built-in light sensor. It connects over 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi with no hub and is powered by USB-C at 5 V, with no battery. Apple Home, Google Home and Alexa support it natively, and Home Assistant uses its HomeKit Device integration. SmartThings is unconfirmed, and Matter isn't confirmed either.
caveats: 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi only; WPA/WPA2 enterprise networks are not supported.
It appears as several separate sensors, and third-party platforms get only basic sensor data.
Fall detection works only in ceiling mode.
Full local automation needs an Aqara hub with Wi-Fi, per the manual.
